This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

VU Biomedical Sciences studies human health and disease from molecules and cells to organs and populations. Its bachelor combines genetics, cell biology, biochemistry, immunity, anatomy and physiology with research methods and practical work. The third year includes open minor space, a restricted choice and a substantial supervised research thesis.

UCR offers three qualified related directions: human biology and disease with research methods; biomedicine and population-health prevention; and biomedical foundations with data analysis. Each retains substantial biological and disease content. General social, economics and computing courses support the chosen emphasis; they do not guarantee specialist biomedical projects. Histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the prolonged VU research placement remain important gaps.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Ordinary bachelor; Experimental thesis selected

The 180 EC comprises 108 EC prescribed first- and second-year courses, three separate 6 EC restricted choices, 30 EC open minor space and one 24 EC thesis. The first-listed choices are shown; other minor and thesis options are not stacked. Thesis entry requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 42 EC from year two, an approved project and completed registration. A go/no-go review, scientific report, oral and poster presentations and sufficient research performance apply. The usual first-year study advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to applicable exceptions. Lab safety and the Dutch language test or required remediation are mandatory without extra credit. Programme instruction changed to Dutch in 2026; individual courses may be English.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Biomedical Sciences at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Human biology, disease and research methods

Combines molecular cell biology, biochemistry, human physiology, genetics and pathology with infection and immunity, pharmacology, laboratory study and neuroscience. General statistics and evidence synthesis support research literacy. This provides substantive biomedical foundations while leaving gaps in specialist histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the prolonged VU research placement.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Biomedicine, population health and prevention

Combines substantial molecular, physiological, genetic and disease study with epidemiology, health psychology, qualitative and quantitative methods, sociology, ethics and communication. It develops a related population-health and prevention direction. General social and economics courses are contextual contributions; a dedicated global-health policy or health-systems programme is not supplied.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Biomedical foundations and data analysis

Combines molecular, physiological, genetic and disease foundations with statistics, programming, data analysis, numerical methods and machine learning. Actual medical-image processing and quantitative pharmacology give specific biomedical applications. General computing courses do not guarantee biomedical datasets, and this is not a dedicated omics, bioinformatics or clinical prediction-validation sequence.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Public Economics
Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Linear Algebra
Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and applications including Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains.
Close

Computational & Numerical Methods
Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.
Close

Linear Systems
Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.
Close

Probability & Statistics
Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Epidemiology & Public Health
Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.
Close

Functional Anatomy
Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through surface anatomy, medical imaging, scientific drawing, dissection-related materials and clinical demonstrations. These are academic learning activities rather than clinical skills training.
Close

Pharmacology
Covers the science of drugs—their origin, composition, kinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity. Discusses drug targets, interactions and kinetics, enabling students to explain therapies in terms of molecular targets and physiological consequences.
Close

Infection & Immunity
Explores fundamental processes in immunology such as recognition of self vs non‑self, lymphocyte receptor development and innate and adaptive immune responses. Examines host‑pathogen interactions, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology.
Close

Mechanisms of Disease
Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. It connects embryology, anatomy and physiology with symptoms and failures in the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine and central nervous systems.
Close

Neurobiology
Neurobiology studies the biological basis of behaviour through evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy, animal models and selected disorders. Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Perception & Action
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Close

Higher Order Functions
Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision-making and planning. Students evaluate current research and develop experimental designs.
Close

Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
Introduces cells, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication. It connects genetic information and variation with living systems and offers initial perspectives on life sciences, biomedicine and public health. A research presentation develops engagement with scientific literature.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Molecular Cell Biology
Provides foundation for practical applications in life science. Focuses on cellular biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes, revisits concepts from introductory courses, examines current research and encourages evaluating reproducibility and modernising methods.
Close

Human Physiology
Studies normal functioning of the human body, covering structure‑function relationships, energy handling, homeostasis, signalling, organ systems and integration of their functions.
Close

Biochemistry
Explores the chemistry of life and biomolecules such as proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids. Discusses metabolic pathways, the role of biomolecules in health and disease and applications in medicine, biotechnology and sustainability.
Close

Life Science Laboratory
Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.
Close

Molecular Pathology & Genetics
Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Medical & Health Psychology
Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Perception & Action
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Close

Higher Order Functions
Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision-making and planning. Students evaluate current research and develop experimental designs.
Close

Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
Introduces cells, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication. It connects genetic information and variation with living systems and offers initial perspectives on life sciences, biomedicine and public health. A research presentation develops engagement with scientific literature.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Molecular Cell Biology
Provides foundation for practical applications in life science. Focuses on cellular biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes, revisits concepts from introductory courses, examines current research and encourages evaluating reproducibility and modernising methods.
Close

Human Physiology
Studies normal functioning of the human body, covering structure‑function relationships, energy handling, homeostasis, signalling, organ systems and integration of their functions.
Close

Biochemistry
Explores the chemistry of life and biomolecules such as proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids. Discusses metabolic pathways, the role of biomolecules in health and disease and applications in medicine, biotechnology and sustainability.
Close

Life Science Laboratory
Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.
Close

Molecular Pathology & Genetics
Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Medical & Health Psychology
Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
